title: Pre-Dilation Before Fundus Exam

patient.name: Mdm Wong Ah Mui
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for dilated fundus examination — diabetic eye screening

history.hpc: Mdm Wong is a 72-year-old diabetic referred from her GP for a dilated fundus examination as part of her annual diabetic eye screening. She has no current eye complaints — no pain, no redness, vision 'still okay' with glasses. She has never had dilation before.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 15 years. Hypertension. No previous eye surgery.
history.social_hx: Does not drive. Came with daughter today.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: No contraindications to dilation observed. Pupils normal and reactive.
examination_findings.fundus: Fundus cannot be adequately assessed without dilation — assessment to follow after drops take effect

investigations.va_distance: Measured with habitual correction (glasses). RE: LogMAR 0.3. LE: LogMAR 0.2.
investigations.iop_nct: RE: 15 mmHg. LE: 14 mmHg. IOP measured before dilation as per protocol.
investigations.dilation: Tropicamide 1% one drop each eye instilled at 10:00am. Second drop instilled at 10:05am. Patient advised to wait 20-30 minutes.

diagnosis: Diabetic patient requiring dilated fundus examination. No contraindication to dilation identified. Standard pre-dilation protocol applied.

immediate: Confirm correct patient identity (full name and NRIC) before instilling any drops
Explain procedure and obtain verbal consent
Check for known allergies to eye drops
Warn patient: vision will be blurred and eye sensitive to light for 4-6 hours after dilation
Instil tropicamide 1% — one drop per eye, wait 5 minutes, then second drop per eye
Ask patient to sit in waiting area for 20-30 minutes
Document drop name, dosage, time instilled, and by whom
follow_up: Recheck pupils after 20-30 minutes to confirm dilation adequate
Escort patient to doctor when dilation achieved
Doctor to perform dilated fundus examination
patient_education: Advise not to drive after dilation — patient should have someone escort her home
Sunglasses recommended outdoors after dilation due to light sensitivity
Explain dilation is temporary and vision will return to normal after 4-6 hours

key_points: Confirms patient identity correctly before instilling drops
Asks about known allergies to eye drops
Asks whether patient is driving today (cannot drive after dilation)
Explains procedure and gets verbal consent before instilling drops
Measures VA before dilation (both distance and near if required)
Correct technique for eye drop instillation: lower lid retracted, drop in conjunctival sac, patient looks up, one drop at a time, nasolacrimal occlusion advised
Documents drop name, concentration, time, and number of drops
Does not instil drops without checking allergies and identity
Recognises that driving after dilation is unsafe
Uses correct drop (tropicamide 1%) and correct technique
Waits correct time between drops (5 minutes) and before reassessment (20-30 minutes)
Educates patient on post-dilation care (no driving, light sensitivity, duration)
